EN: The simple straight line example makes it seem easy, but space has more dimensions. Over time you will \nsee the correlation of this basic principle in every facet of orbital maneuvering.
Everything about moving in space is about changing your vessel's velocity. Each maneuver is an equation \nwhere you trade fuel for velocity, and this is measured in delta-v.
Delta-v (or Δv for short) is a measure of the impulse needed by a vessel to perform a maneuver.

Every maneuver you make uses propellant, and rockets have a finite supply. Choosing the best time (or 
place) to make maneuvers determines whether you complete your mission, or have to get out and push. 
Maneuver nodes are really useful in this situation, they help you see the "cost" of maneuvers before 
executing them.

Matching planes is a key maneuver involved in docking. The best place to do this is at the orbit nodes \nlabelled Ascending/Descending Node (AN/DN). When you select a target object these indicate where your \nvessel and the target's orbital planes cross.
